name: Chunk size experiment for technical chats

content.text: Compare chunk sizes for technical chats and tell me what changed when the team focused on retrieval tuning instead of swapping to a bigger model.
I should contrast 350, 700, and 1200 character chunks, mention lost anchor terms, and explain why narrower chunks helped retrieval more than swapping to a bigger model.

Chunk size experiment for technical chats: 350 to 500 character chunks improved precision because each retrieval unit stayed focused on one troubleshooting idea. At 1200 characters the search started mixing benchmark notes, deployment caveats, and unrelated prompts in the same chunk. That made the final answer more likely to hallucinate, even though the generation model never changed.
Can you turn that into a release note style summary with a clear recommendation?
Keep it concise, stress that retrieval tuning beat model scaling, and keep the wording suitable for docs screenshots.

Recommendation: prefer smaller, semantically coherent chunks for technical chat archives, then add reranking before you consider a larger generation model. In this test set, better chunking reduced hallucinations more reliably than upgrading the model because the answer prompt was grounded in sharper evidence from the local index.
